sms.title: SMS commands
sms.description: What to send by SMS to which truck. Send a text from your phone to the truck's SIM number; the unit answers to the phone that sent it.
sms.syntax: Every text has the form command#password[#parameters].
sms.caseInsensitive: Commands and the password are case-insensitive.
sms.maxBytes: A text to the unit may be at most 64 bytes; the unit does not accept a longer one.
sms.replyTo: The unit sends its reply to the phone number that sent the command.
sms.noPasswordHint: No Simple SMS password is stored for this device, so its texts cannot be prepared. Add the password (parameter 0593) in the device editor.
sms.copyByHand: The browser did not allow copying. The text is selected: press Ctrl+C, or tap Copy on a phone.

sms.firstDevices: The Branch has {total} devices; this page lists the first {shown}.
sms.karmaWarning: Emergency only. After these texts the unit reports to Karma, and DiscoCan receives none of its data until you route it back to DiscoCan.

check.title: Check the unit
check.description: These texts only read; they change nothing on the unit. Use them to see whether the unit answers and which server it reports to.

route.title: Route to DiscoCan
route.description: Makes DiscoCan (65.108.137.165, port 11500) the unit's primary server. Send the two texts in this order and send the second one only after the reply ok#setparam to the first. About 10 minutes later check the result with getparam 49 and 50. If the unit does not come online, call its SIM number to wake it.

karma.title: Emergency: back to Karma
karma.description: Makes Karma (in.karma.online, port 500) the unit's primary server again. Send the two texts in this order and send the second one only after the reply ok#setparam to the first.

info.when: To see that the unit is alive and answers SMS, and to read its model, serial number, firmware, GSM operator and signal, IP address and voltages.
info.reply: One line such as StarLink-CT 2e1-XL #02A23F 2.34; 05/11 06:22; "ORANGE" (425001) …; the fields depend on the firmware.

loc.when: To see where the truck is when it is not online. The unit answers with its last known position and does not switch GNSS on for it.
loc.reply: Event: Location; In: …; Out: …; LocTime: …; Speed: …; Link: http://maps.google.com/?q=…

getparam49.when: To see which server the unit sends its data to.
getparam49.reply: 65.108.137.165 when the unit is routed to DiscoCan; in.karma.online when it reports to Karma.

getparam50.reply: 11500 when the unit is routed to DiscoCan; 500 when it reports to Karma.

getparam51.when: To check the backup server that the unit uses when its primary server does not answer.

getparam52.reply: 500, the port of the Karma backup server.

route49.purpose: Step 1: DiscoCan's address as the primary server
route49.when: The first text when you route the unit to DiscoCan.

route50.when: Send it after the reply to step 1.
route50.reply: ok#setparam. The unit then connects to DiscoCan.

karma49.purpose: Step 1: Karma's address as the primary server

karma50.when: Send it after the reply to step 1.
karma50.reply: ok#setparam. The unit then reports to Karma again.

branchQueue.title: Command queue
branchQueue.body: This page lists requests for devices in the selected fleet and their status: queued, sent, completed or failed. Parameter reads and changes also appear as commands. Batch requests run separately for each device.

overview.title: Device overview
overview.body: The overview shows the device connection, route and latest reports. Vehicle readings, warning lamps and location come from received reports. The GPS position time may differ from the last connection time.

problems.title: Device problems
problems.body: This tab shows current warnings and the history of reported problems. Each record identifies the source, time and problem status. A missing report does not prove that the device or vehicle has no faults.

commands.title: Device commands
commands.body: Commands are queued requests sent to the device, with statuses including queued, sent, completed and failed. Parameters are the settings stored in the device itself. Every parameter read or change also passes through the queue as a command.

smsCommands.title: SMS commands
smsCommands.body: This tab prepares SMS text for the selected device using its SIM number and password. Messages are sent from a phone, rather than from this page. Device replies are not added automatically to the DiscoCan queue.

parameters.title: Device parameters
parameters.body: Parameters are settings stored in the device and read together in one operation. The history retains the values and differences between reads. Command 46 makes one controlled change at a time, followed by a read to verify it. Every read or change also passes through the command queue, where its progress is tracked.

events.title: Device events
events.body: Events are decoded reports received from the device. The history can be sorted by time, type and severity, and filtered by one or several severities. Filters and sorting are kept in the URL and apply to the entire history.

frames.title: Device frames
frames.body: Frames are protocol messages received from or sent to the device. Each record shows its direction, time, checksum and content. This history supports technical inspection of device communication.
